concepts.name: problem
concepts.description: A new situation that requires a solution.

concepts.name: case
concepts.description: A stored experience consisting of a problem and a solution that can be reused.

concepts.name: caseMemory
concepts.description: A memory store of prior cases available for retrieval.

concepts.name: solution
concepts.description: A candidate answer or validated response to a problem.

concepts.name: retrievalMethod
concepts.description: A strategy for finding relevant prior cases.

concepts.name: adaptationMethod
concepts.description: A strategy for modifying a retrieved case to fit a new problem.

concepts.name: evaluationMethod
concepts.description: A strategy for judging whether a candidate solution works.

concepts.name: similarity
concepts.description: A measure of how closely two problems or cases are related.

concepts.name: heuristic
concepts.description: A rule of thumb used to guide adaptation when exact reasoning is too costly.

concepts.name: model
concepts.description: Domain knowledge or a world model that can support case adaptation.

concepts.name: subgoal
concepts.description: An intermediate goal created when a problem is decomposed into smaller parts.

concepts.name: caseBasedReasoning
concepts.description: A problem-solving method that reuses stored cases from memory.

concepts.name: configuration
concepts.description: The current state or context of a problem-solving situation.

assertions.name: patternRecurrenceAssumption
assertions.description: Case-based reasoning assumes that similar problems recur and can be handled by reusing prior experience.

assertions.name: similarProblemsSimilarSolutions
assertions.description: A common assumption is that similar problems tend to have similar solutions, although this is not always true.

assertions.name: smallAdaptationTweak
assertions.description: Adaptation often involves small changes to a retrieved case rather than reconstructing a solution from scratch.

assertions.name: goodCaseBasedSolution
assertions.description: A good case-based solution is retrieved, adapted, evaluated, and then stored as a new case for future use.
